app.name: Calcora
app.tagline: Plan smarter with calculators built for your country
gate.title: Welcome to {app}
gate.subtitle: Tell us where you are and how you'd like to read. Rules, currency and tax logic all follow your country.
gate.country.title: Choose your country
gate.country.subtitle: Calculators, currency and tax rules are country specific.
gate.language.title: Choose your language
gate.language.subtitle: Every page on {app} is shown in the language you pick.
gate.note: You can change both at any time from the header.
home.title: Calculators
home.subtitle: {count} free calculators using {country} rules, rates and currency.
home.empty: No calculators are available for this country yet.
calc.notAvailable: This calculator is not available for {country}.
calc.mortgage.title: Mortgage Calculator
calc.mortgage.desc: Work out the monthly payment on a home loan and what it costs in total.
calc.mortgage.note: Property tax, insurance, fees and any rate reset during the term are not included.
calc.mortgage.explain: The payment is level for the whole term. Early payments are mostly interest, and the share going to the principal grows every month - the breakdown table shows exactly when that crosses over for your figures.
calc.auto-loan.title: Auto Loan Calculator
calc.auto-loan.desc: Calculate the monthly payment and total interest on a car loan.
calc.auto-loan.explain: A larger down payment cuts both the amount borrowed and the interest charged on it. Shorter terms raise the monthly payment but lower the total cost.
calc.loan.title: Loan Calculator
calc.loan.desc: Monthly payment, total interest and payoff schedule for any loan.
calc.loan.explain: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, which falls a little with every payment. The level payment splits differently each month as a result.
calc.loan.faq.1.q: Does paying extra reduce the interest?
calc.loan.faq.1.a: Yes. Anything paid above the scheduled amount goes straight to the principal, which cuts both the balance and all the interest that would have accrued on it.
calc.loan.faq.2.q: Why does the interest barely fall in the first years?
calc.loan.faq.2.a: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, which is at its highest at the start. The breakdown table shows the crossover year for your figures.
calc.student-loan.title: Student Loan Calculator
calc.student-loan.desc: See what a student loan costs to repay and how long it takes.
calc.student-loan.explain: This treats the loan as a fixed repayment plan. Income-contingent systems instead take a share of what you earn, and any balance left at the end of the term is written off.
calc.student-loan.note.generic: Assumes a fixed repayment schedule at a constant rate.
calc.student-loan.note.incomeContingent: Repayments here are income-contingent in practice: you pay a share of earnings above a threshold, not a fixed instalment, and the balance is written off after the statutory period.
calc.income-tax.title: Income Tax Calculator
calc.income-tax.desc: Estimate the tax on your annual income and what you keep after it.
calc.income-tax.explain.1: Income is reduced by the allowances and deductions you qualify for, then the remainder is taxed band by band - each rate applies only to the income inside its own band.
calc.income-tax.explain.2: The effective rate is total tax over gross income. The marginal rate is what the next unit of income would be taxed at.
calc.income-tax.faq.1.q: Why is my effective rate lower than my band rate?
calc.income-tax.faq.1.a: Because only the income above each threshold is taxed at that band's rate. The income below it is taxed at the lower rates, so the average always lands under the top rate you reach.
calc.income-tax.faq.2.a: No. This covers the main allowances and the standard deduction. Special reliefs, credits and local taxes are not modelled, so treat the result as an estimate.
calc.income-tax.status.head: Head of household
calc.income-tax.hint.in: Section 80C, 80D, home loan interest and the rest, combined.
calc.income-tax.hint.us: Itemised deductions. They replace the standard deduction only if they exceed it.
calc.income-tax.hint.gb: Pension contributions and other allowable deductions.
calc.income-tax.hint.ca: RRSP contributions and other deductions from income.
calc.income-tax.hint.de: Werbungskosten and Sonderausgaben above the standard allowance.
calc.income-tax.hint.ch: Pillar 3a contributions and other allowable deductions.
calc.income-tax.hint.fr: Deductible expenses beyond the automatic 10% allowance.
calc.income-tax.hint.nl: Deductible items such as mortgage interest.
calc.income-tax.hint.jp: Insurance premiums, dependants and other deductions.
calc.income-tax.hint.mx: Deducciones personales such as medical costs and mortgage interest.
calc.income-tax.hint.pt: Deductible expenses beyond the automatic allowance.
calc.income-tax.hint.br: Legal deductions, if you itemise instead of taking the simplified allowance.
calc.income-tax.note.in: Salaried figures for FY 2025-26, including the standard deduction, the Section 87A rebate and 4% cess.
calc.income-tax.note.us: Federal tax and FICA for 2025. State and local income taxes are not included.
calc.income-tax.note.gb: England, Wales and Northern Ireland for 2025/26, including Class 1 National Insurance. Scotland uses different bands.
calc.income-tax.note.ae: The UAE charges no personal income tax on salary income, so take-home pay equals gross pay.
calc.income-tax.note.ca: Federal tax, CPP and EI for 2025. Provincial income tax is not included and adds materially to the total.
calc.income-tax.note.au: Resident rates for 2025-26 plus the Medicare levy. Offsets such as LITO are not included.
calc.income-tax.note.de: Tax class I for 2025 under the §32a schedule, with employee social contributions. Social contributions are not deducted as Vorsorgeaufwendungen, so the taxable income shown is higher than on a real assessment. Church tax is calculated separately.
calc.income-tax.note.at: 2025 rates with employee social insurance. Absetzbeträge are not included.
calc.income-tax.note.ch: Federal direct tax only. Cantonal and communal taxes usually exceed the federal amount and are not included.
calc.income-tax.note.fr: 2025 barème for a single share. The quotient familial for couples and dependants is not modelled.
calc.income-tax.note.be: 2025 rates including an indicative 7% communal surcharge. Regional differences are not modelled.
calc.income-tax.note.nl: Box 1 for 2025, below state pension age, with the general and labour tax credits applied.
calc.income-tax.note.jp: National tax, the 2.1% reconstruction surtax and a flat 10% resident tax, with employment income and basic deductions.
calc.income-tax.note.es: State scale plus an indicative regional scale for 2025. Your autonomous community's rates will differ.
calc.income-tax.note.mx: 2025 annual ISR tariff. The subsidio para el empleo is not included.
calc.income-tax.note.it: IRPEF for 2025 with indicative regional and municipal surcharges, which vary by comune.
calc.income-tax.note.pt: Mainland Portugal for 2025, single taxpayer without dependants.
calc.income-tax.note.br: IRPF annualised from the 2025 monthly table using the simplified deduction, plus INSS.
calc.income-tax.note.pl: 2025 PIT scale for an employment contract, with ZUS and health contributions.
calc.income-tax.note.tr: 2025 tariff with SGK and unemployment contributions. The minimum wage exemption is not applied.
calc.salary.title: Salary Calculator
calc.salary.desc: Turn a gross salary into take-home pay after tax and contributions.
calc.salary.explain: Gross pay is reduced first by income tax and then by the statutory contributions your country charges on earnings. What is left is what actually reaches your account.
calc.vat.title: {tax} Calculator
calc.vat.desc: Add or remove {tax} from any amount and see the split.
calc.vat.explain: On a tax-exclusive amount the tax is added on top. On a tax-inclusive amount it is worked back out, which is why dividing by the rate is not the same as multiplying by it.
calc.vat.faq.1.q: How do I get the pre-tax price from a final price?
calc.vat.faq.1.a: Switch the amount type to “Tax already included”. The calculator divides by one plus the rate, which is the only correct way to reverse it.
calc.vat.note.in: Within a state GST splits equally into CGST and SGST; across states the same total is charged as IGST.
calc.vat.note.us: Sales tax rates are set by state, county and city, so pick the rate that applies where the sale happens.
calc.vat.note.gb: The standard rate is 20%. Some goods are reduced-rated at 5% and others, including most food and children's clothing, are zero-rated.
calc.vat.note.ca: GST alone is 5%. HST provinces combine it with the provincial share into a single rate, and others charge PST or QST separately.
calc.vat.note.au: GST is 10% and applies to most goods and services, with basic food, health and education GST-free.
calc.vat.note.de: The standard rate is 19%, with 7% for food, books and public transport.
calc.vat.note.at: The standard rate is 20%, with reduced rates of 10% and 13%.
calc.vat.note.ch: The standard rate is 8.1%, with 2.6% for everyday goods and 3.8% for accommodation.
calc.vat.note.fr: The standard rate is 20%, with 10%, 5.5% and 2.1% applying to specific goods and services.
calc.vat.note.be: The standard rate is 21%, with 6% and 12% for specific categories.
calc.vat.note.nl: The standard rate is 21%, with a 9% rate for food, books, medicines and some services.
calc.vat.note.jp: Consumption tax is 10%, with a reduced 8% rate for food and drink other than alcohol and dining out.
calc.vat.note.es: The standard rate is 21%, with 10% and a super-reduced 4% for essentials.
calc.vat.note.mx: IVA is 16% nationally, with a reduced 8% rate in the northern and southern border regions.
calc.vat.note.it: The standard rate is 22%, with 10%, 5% and 4% applying to specific goods.
calc.vat.note.pt: Mainland rates are 23%, 13% and 6%. Madeira and the Azores use lower rates.
calc.vat.note.br: Brazil layers ICMS, ISS, PIS and COFINS rather than charging one VAT. These are common ICMS rates and are a rough guide only.
calc.vat.note.pl: The standard rate is 23%, with 8% and 5% for specific goods.
calc.vat.note.tr: KDV is 20% as standard, with 10% and 1% rates for specific goods.
calc.vat.note.ae: VAT is 5% on most goods and services, with some supplies zero-rated or exempt.
calc.capital-gains.title: Capital Gains Tax Calculator
calc.capital-gains.desc: Estimate the tax on an investment gain and what you keep.
calc.capital-gains.explain: The gain is the sale price less what you paid. How it is taxed depends on how long you held the asset and, in several countries, on the rest of your income.
calc.capital-gains.note.us: Long-term rates apply after twelve months; shorter holdings are taxed as ordinary income. The 3.8% net investment income tax is not included.
calc.capital-gains.note.gb: Uses the 24% rate and the £3,000 annual exempt amount. Basic-rate taxpayers pay 18% on gains within their basic-rate band.
calc.capital-gains.note.ca: Half the gain is taxable and added to income. The marginal rate used here is indicative and excludes provincial tax.
calc.capital-gains.note.au: Assets held over twelve months qualify for the 50% discount; the remainder is taxed at your marginal rate.
calc.capital-gains.note.de: Abgeltungsteuer of 25% plus solidarity surcharge, after the €1,000 saver's allowance. Church tax is not included.
calc.capital-gains.note.fr: The flat 30% prélèvement forfaitaire unique combines 12.8% income tax and 17.2% social levies.
calc.capital-gains.note.es: Gains are taxed on the separate savings scale, which runs from 19% to 28%.
calc.capital-gains.note.it: Financial gains are taxed at a flat 26%, with a lower rate for government bonds.
calc.capital-gains.note.in: Listed equity held over twelve months is taxed at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh of gains; shorter holdings are taxed at 20%.
calc.stamp-duty.title: Stamp Duty Calculator
calc.stamp-duty.desc: Work out the stamp duty land tax on a property purchase.
calc.stamp-duty.explain: Stamp duty is banded like income tax: each rate applies only to the slice of the price inside its band, so the effective rate is always lower than the top band you reach.
calc.stamp-duty.note: England and Northern Ireland rates from April 2025. Scotland charges LBTT and Wales charges LTT, both with different bands.
calc.church-tax.title: Church Tax Calculator
calc.church-tax.desc: Estimate the church tax charged alongside your income tax.
calc.church-tax.explain: Church tax is charged as a percentage of your income tax, not of your income, so it rises and falls with the tax bill rather than with earnings.
calc.church-tax.note: 8% in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, 9% in the other federal states. Leaving the church formally ends the liability.
calc.property-tax.title: Property Tax Calculator
calc.property-tax.desc: Estimate the annual tax charged on a property.
calc.property-tax.explain: Property tax is set locally and charged on an assessed value that often differs from the market price, so treat the rate here as a starting point to replace with your own.
calc.property-tax.note: Rates are set by the local authority and the assessed value is usually below the market price, so check both against your own bill.
calc.retirement.title: Retirement Calculator
calc.retirement.desc: See what your savings could grow to by the time you retire.
calc.retirement.explain: Existing savings and future contributions are projected forward at the expected return, then discounted by inflation to show what the total would actually buy.
calc.retirement.todayHint: What that amount would buy at today's prices.
calc.pension.title: Pension Calculator
calc.pension.desc: Project your pension pot from your own and your employer's contributions.
calc.pension.explain: Contributions are a percentage of salary from both sides, invested until retirement. The 4% figure is a common guideline for a sustainable first-year withdrawal, not a guarantee.
calc.pension.note: State pension entitlements are not included. Contributions are assumed to stay at the same percentage of salary throughout.
calc.401k.title: 401(k) Calculator
calc.401k.desc: Project your 401(k) balance, including the employer match.
calc.401k.explain: The employer match is the highest-return part of the plan: contributing at least up to the match limit takes the full amount on offer.
calc.401k.note: Uses the 2025 elective deferral limit of $23,500. Catch-up contributions from age 50 are not included.
calc.social-security-benefit.title: Social Security Calculator
calc.social-security-benefit.desc: Estimate your monthly Social Security retirement benefit.
calc.social-security-benefit.explain: The benefit is built from average indexed monthly earnings through three bend points, then adjusted for when you claim: earlier means permanently less, later means permanently more.
calc.social-security-benefit.note: A simplified estimate from 2025 bend points and a single average earnings figure. The Social Security Administration uses your highest 35 indexed years.
calc.superannuation.title: Superannuation Calculator
calc.superannuation.desc: Project your super balance from employer and extra contributions.
calc.superannuation.explain: Employer contributions go in at the Superannuation Guarantee rate and are taxed at 15% on the way in. What is left compounds until retirement.
calc.superannuation.note: Uses the 12% Superannuation Guarantee rate from 1 July 2025. Contribution caps and Division 293 tax are not modelled.
calc.hecs.title: HECS-HELP Calculator
calc.hecs.desc: See what your HELP debt costs each year and when it clears.
calc.hecs.explain: HELP repayments are compulsory once income passes the threshold and are taken as a share of earnings. The debt is indexed each year, so repayments race indexation.
calc.hecs.note: Uses the marginal repayment system from 2025-26 with a $67,000 threshold. Indexation is applied before each year's repayment.
calc.social-security.title: Social Security Calculator
calc.social-security.desc: See the social contributions taken from your salary.
calc.social-security.explain: Contributions are charged on gross pay, often only up to a ceiling, and fund pensions, healthcare and unemployment cover. They are separate from income tax.
calc.social-security.note: Employee contributions only. Employer contributions are charged on top and are not shown here.
calc.national-insurance.title: National Insurance Calculator
calc.national-insurance.desc: Work out the National Insurance due on your earnings.
calc.national-insurance.explain: Class 1 National Insurance is charged at 8% on earnings between the primary threshold and the upper earnings limit, then at 2% above it.
calc.national-insurance.note: Class 1 employee rates for 2025/26. Employer National Insurance is charged separately.
calc.cpp.title: CPP Calculator
calc.cpp.desc: Calculate your Canada Pension Plan contributions.
calc.cpp.explain: Contributions run at 5.95% on earnings between the basic exemption and the year's maximum pensionable earnings, with a second tier above that.
calc.cpp.note: 2025 rates, employee share only. Quebec residents contribute to the QPP instead, at a higher rate.
calc.ei.title: EI Calculator
calc.ei.explain: EI premiums are charged at a flat rate on insurable earnings up to the annual maximum, after which nothing further is due for the year.
calc.ei.note: 2025 rates, employee share only. Quebec has a separate rate because of its parental insurance plan.
calc.30-percent-ruling.title: 30% Ruling Calculator
calc.30-percent-ruling.desc: See what the Dutch 30% ruling is worth to you each year.
calc.30-percent-ruling.explain: Under the ruling part of your salary is paid free of tax, which cuts your taxable income and moves the rest into lower brackets. The benefit is the difference in net pay.
calc.30-percent-ruling.note: The exemption applies up to the capped salary. Eligibility, the five-year maximum and the scheduled reduction to 27% are not modelled here.
calc.payroll.title: Payroll Calculator
calc.payroll.desc: See the full cost of employing someone, from gross pay to employer charges.
calc.payroll.explain: The employer pays more than the gross salary: social charges sit on top, while tax and employee contributions come out of the gross to give take-home pay.
calc.payroll.note: Employer charges here are indicative averages. Actual rates depend on sector, headcount and insurance choices.
calc.severance-pay.title: Severance Pay Calculator
calc.severance-pay.desc: Calculate severance and notice pay under Turkish labour law.
calc.severance-pay.explain: Severance is one month's gross pay for each year of service, capped per year at the statutory ceiling. Notice pay is separate and rises in steps with tenure.
calc.severance-pay.capHint: The statutory ceiling per year of service.
calc.severance-pay.note: Severance is exempt from income tax but bears stamp duty. Entitlement requires at least one year of service and a qualifying reason for leaving.
calc.tip.title: Tip Calculator
calc.tip.desc: Split a bill and work out the tip per person.
calc.tip.explain: The tip is a percentage of the bill before it is divided, so everyone contributes the same share of both.
calc.inflation.title: Inflation Calculator
calc.inflation.desc: See what an amount will cost later, or what it is worth today.
calc.inflation.explain: Inflation compounds: a steady rate has a small effect over a year and a large one over a decade, which is why long-horizon plans have to account for it.
calc.sip.title: SIP Calculator
calc.sip.desc: See what a fixed monthly investment could grow into over time.
calc.sip.stepUpHint: Raise the instalment by this much every year.
calc.sip.explain.1: Each instalment is invested at the start of the month and compounds monthly at the expected rate, so early instalments do the heaviest lifting.
calc.sip.explain.2: The expected return is an assumption, not a promise. Market-linked investments can and do return less, including less than you put in.
calc.sip.faq.1.a: No. It is the rate you assume for the projection. Actual returns depend on how the underlying investments perform.
calc.sip.faq.2.q: What happens if I stop paying midway?
calc.sip.faq.2.a: Contributions stop but the balance stays invested and keeps compounding. Re-run the calculator with the number of years you actually contributed to see the difference.
footer.disclaimer: Calcora's calculators are for illustration only. Results are estimates, not financial or tax advice. Verify figures with a qualified professional before acting on them.
error.notFoundBody: The calculator you're looking for may have moved or isn't offered in this country.
